title: Out of the red zone
topic: On ExxonMobil's automated drilling rigs in Midland, three robot arms from Helmerich and Payne now move and connect heavy drill pipe on the rig floor, while the crew runs them from a small office on the rig.

treatment.logline: Open up a Midland rig floor and watch the heaviest, closest work move from a floorhand's gloved hands to a robot arm with a face, while the same crew climbs into the doghouse to run it.
treatment.cold_open: A tall joint of pipe swings in over the hole and the floorhand reaches with greasy gloves, then pulls both hands back as the orange pipe arm swings in, blinks and takes it.
treatment.turn: The test at full strength. Exxon expects similar staffing and believes the robots could prevent a third of serious incidents, and the film draws both as company expectations, a dashed tag and a raised brow, not counts.
treatment.button: Who tightens the pipe now? The arm spins the next joint tight below the window, the gloves hang still on the peg, and a bare hand taps go.

hero.name: the pipe arm
hero.why: an orange pipe-handling robot with a face on its shoulder housing, the machine the story is about, drawn fresh for this film

scenes.vo: In Midland, a column of drill pipe over two stories tall swings toward the hole. The floorhand pulls back both gloves, because a robot arm already has it.

draw.subject: the pipe arm
draw.action: swings a tall joint of pipe in over the hole

draw.subject: a height marker
draw.action: climbs the joint to show it towers two floorhands high

draw.subject: the floorhand
draw.action: pulls both greasy gloves back from a joint that towers two floorhands high

draw.subject: the pipe arm
draw.action: closes its jaws on the pipe and blinks at the floorhand

scenes.vo: On this ExxonMobil rig, robotic arms set the pipe in place and connect it to the drill string. Crews on the floor used to help do that by hand.

draw.subject: the pipe arm
draw.action: stabs the joint down onto the pipe in the slips

visual_events.at_phrase: connect it to the drill string
visual_events.label: Drill string

draw.subject: the pipe arm
draw.action: turns the joint in its jaws and makes up the connection

draw.subject: two ghost floorhands
draw.action: fade in where they once stood, wrestling the tongs

scenes.vo: So the floor gets a fence. The gate carries a sign that reads Red Zone, with a drawing of the Grim Reaper.

draw.subject: the gate
draw.action: slides shut around the rig floor in front of the floorhand

draw.subject: the Red Zone sign
draw.action: swings on its wires as the floorhand leans in to read it

scenes.vo: Exxon's Bart Cahir says about a third of significant drilling injuries have happened right here, on the rig floor.

draw.subject: three red injury tags
draw.action: drop onto a glass map of the rig while the Exxon executive points

draw.subject: one of the three tags
draw.action: slides onto the rig floor on the map and glows red

scenes.vo: Drilling contractor Helmerich and Payne supplies the system. Three arms move pipe weighing roughly 2,000 pounds. One walks each stand to the hole, one lines up the threads, and one racks pipe high in the derrick.

draw.subject: three robot arms
draw.action: unfold one after another across the rig floor

draw.subject: the three arms
draw.action: light their visors one after another and nod

draw.subject: a hook scale
draw.action: swings its needle up to 2,000 lb as the pipe arm lifts

draw.subject: the first arm
draw.action: walks a stand of pipe across to the hole

draw.subject: the second arm
draw.action: wipes the pin and lines it up over the box

draw.subject: the third arm
draw.action: racks a stand into the fingerboard high in the derrick

scenes.vo: So where did the crew go? Up into a small office on the rig, where a contractor runs the robots with controls on a screen.

draw.subject: the floorhand
draw.action: climbs the stairs up to the doghouse

draw.subject: the gloves
draw.action: get pulled off and hung on a peg by the doghouse door

draw.subject: the screens
draw.action: light up blue across the floorhand's face

scenes.vo: That contractor is the driller, who starts each move and watches it, and the arms follow paths planned in advance. The crew works out the exact moves with an Exxon operations team in Houston.

draw.subject: the driller
draw.action: presses start and the arm on screen follows a dotted path

draw.subject: the dotted path
draw.action: draws itself ahead of the arm and the arm rides it

draw.subject: a line
draw.action: runs from Midland to Houston and an engineer waves back on screen

scenes.vo: Exxon runs more than 30 rigs in the Permian, and in August, Reuters counted two that were automated. Exxon plans to automate more than half its unconventional fleet by the end of 2028.

draw.subject: more than 30 derricks
draw.action: pop up across the plain in rows

draw.subject: two derricks
draw.action: light up orange with a tick badge

draw.subject: the unconventional fleet on the tablet
draw.action: lights orange row by row past the halfway line

scenes.vo: The first one already set a pace. It drilled two miles sideways underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history.

draw.subject: the bit
draw.action: turns down under the rig and then runs sideways through the rock

draw.subject: six suns
draw.action: tick on one by one in the sky above the rig

draw.subject: a podium
draw.action: rises with the little rig landing on the third step

scenes.vo: Does a robot take a job? Exxon expects similar staffing, and calls it a force multiplier, not a replacement. It also believes it could prevent roughly a third of high-consequence incidents. Both are company expectations, not counts.

visual_events.label: Does a robot take a job?

draw.subject: the floorhand
draw.action: reads Exxon's line on a tablet and raises one brow

draw.subject: the crew's hard hats
draw.action: line up on the doghouse bench, the same row as before

draw.subject: Exxon's line on the tablet
draw.action: lights up as the floorhand taps it

draw.subject: a future incident report
draw.action: fades to a pale dashed outline on the safety board

draw.subject: a stamp
draw.action: lands on the tablet reading EXPECTED

scenes.vo: Cahir says people off the floor can plan the next operation instead. So who tightens the pipe now? A robot arm does. A person still decides when.

draw.action: sketches the next operation on the screen with a bare hand

draw.subject: a question mark
draw.action: pops up over the pipe on the screen

draw.subject: the pipe arm
draw.action: spins the next joint tight below the window and winks

draw.subject: the driller
draw.action: nods and taps go with a bare hand while the gloves hang still on the peg
